log: Gordon had nine points in 27 minutes as a starter. The show said his usage rate has dropped and he has fallen off this season.
Aaron Gordon played just 24 minutes in Denver's loss, and the show is comfortable moving on from him.
Aaron Nesmith played 33 minutes as a starter on November 13. The show said he stays worth rostering until Tyrese Haliburton returns.
The show said Aaron Nesmith has a secure starting role and can play 34 minutes, though some nights he plays closer to 28. He started and played 33 and 36 minutes in his last two games.
Aaron Wiggins played 24 minutes off the bench for seven points. The show said his minutes and usage are down and he is only playing about 24 minutes a night now.

The show said Atlanta will be without CJ McCollum, Kingston Flemings, Jock Landale and Asa Newell on 11/18, so the starting lineup is unclear. The show expects more minutes and usage for Dyson Daniels, Aaron Wiggins and Luguentz Dort and said Atlanta could start Wiggins even though it prefers him off the bench. The show liked Wiggins and Dort at about $4.4K in a matchup that gives up spot-up shots, and said to watch who starts.

Ace Bailey has started and played 32, 35 and 31 minutes over Utah's last three games with Markkanen out. He scored 42.25 DraftKings points on Nov. 11, and the show said he has a real role and will play a ton of minutes.
Bailey had 18 points, seven rebounds, two steals and four blocks in 31 minutes. The show said he can be played until Jaren Jackson Jr. returns, and that George's return will hurt him a little.

Ace Bailey has started every Utah game while Lauri Markkanen has been out with a right hand fracture, and he played 30 to 35 minutes in each game since November 8. The show said things are only getting better for Bailey with Markkanen out, though it expects him to be inconsistent.

Bailey took only seven shots in 30 minutes on November 15 even though Utah is missing several key players. The show said he needs to be the clear third option behind Keyonte George and Darryn Peterson with double-digit shot attempts.

Ace Bailey played 23 minutes in a 25-point win against LAC on Tuesday, 10 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 5 minutes of garbage time. His 18.2 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

Aday Mara moved into the starting lineup and played 32 minutes with 11 points, six rebounds, and a block. The show said his production was average and he will lose minutes when Ajay Mitchell and Jalen Williams return.

Aday Mara started at power forward on November 13 and played 21 minutes, but the show said he did not start the second half, when Alex Caruso came in and Kenrich Williams moved up to the four. The show said the double-big lineup struggled, that Mara was a minus-20 in a one-point loss, and that the smaller lineup was better. It said Ajay Mitchell's absence was the reason for the Williams and Mara lineup.

Aday Mara played 26 minutes off the bench on November 15 with 16 points and 13 rebounds. The show said some of that came from the blowout and some from minutes that bounce around, since he has moved between starting and the bench. The show said he still needs to be rostered.

The show said AJ Dybantsa is a tough play at $6,600 because he shares the scoring load with Kyshawn George, Anthony Davis and Trae Young. Dybantsa had 13 points and 23.5 DK points in 34 minutes on Nov 11.
AJ Dybantsa started and played 44 minutes against Detroit but scored only 5 points. The show said he still had the best plus-minus on the team and is still learning as a rookie.

AJ Dybantsa scored 12.2 of his 28.2 DraftKings points in garbage time of a 28-point loss against HOU on Sunday, when the lead was 20 or more late. His line is bigger than his normal role; expect less in a close game.
AJ Dybantsa scored 16 points on 18 shots with a high usage rate. The show said his production has been middling and his shooting has been poor.

AJ Dybantsa has started every game and played 30 to 44 minutes over his last eight games. The show said he is off his minutes limit and should play close to 40 minutes against Memphis, and it preferred him to Kyshawn George.

Ajay Mitchell is starting for an Oklahoma City team missing Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace, and he played 28 minutes on 11/10. The show said nobody is coming to take his role soon because the Thunder are so injured.

Ajay Mitchell is questionable with a left ankle sprain, and Oklahoma City is still without Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Jaylin Williams at the Clippers. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has scored 26 to 31 points in each of his last four games.
Ajay Mitchell returned from a sprained ankle on November 15 after missing the November 13 game, and he started and played 27 minutes. The show called him a full start going forward.
Al Horford sat Monday, Nov. 2, for rest on the second night of a back-to-back, not an injury, and is available Thursday.

Al Horford started over Will Richard, but he went scoreless in 14 minutes and came off the bench in the second half. Charles Bassey started the second half instead, and the show said Steve Kerr will keep mixing lineups.
Al Horford is questionable Wednesday at Dallas for low back injury management.

Horford has started two of Golden State's last five games but has played only 13, 15, 21, 10 and 14 minutes in that span, including 14 minutes in his start on 11/16. The show said his minimum $3,500 price is the only thing making him a value, and it said it would rather see Charles Bassey or De'Anthony Melton start.

Caruso returned on Nov. 4 after missing four games and played 20 minutes off the bench with seven points. The show said he should carve out his own role with Cason Wallace and Jalen Williams likely out for the season and Chet Holmgren sidelined.

Alex Caruso moved into the starting lineup with Ajay Mitchell out and played 29 minutes on a back-to-back for 14 points, seven rebounds, three steals, and four threes. Kenrich Williams went to the bench. The show said Ajay Mitchell's ankle injury may not be significant, and Mitchell and Jalen Williams will cut into Caruso's role when they return.

The show listed Alex Caruso as a short-term pickup while Ajay Mitchell is out. With Mitchell sidelined by a right ankle sprain, Caruso started on November 11 and played 29 minutes, then came off the bench for 27 minutes on November 13 when Kenrich Williams started.

Caruso started on Nov 11 and played 29 minutes, then came off the bench for 27 and 18 minutes in his next two games. The show said a lot of guard minutes are up for grabs in Oklahoma City, so it would hold him through a bad game.
Alex Karaban played 29 minutes and went scoreless while Sacramento was without Zach LaVine and De'Andre Hunter. The show called him the worst pick in his draft class.
Alex Morales played 29 minutes off the bench Tuesday at Sacramento with Paolo Banchero, Jalen Suggs, Jonathan Isaac and Tristan da Silva all out.
Alex Morales, a two-way player, made his first NBA start after Jamal Cain was injured. He played 18 minutes and scored five points. Jase Richardson stayed on the bench for 20 minutes.
He is questionable with left knee soreness, and Deandre Ayton started at center in his place Monday and played 24 minutes.

Alex Sarr had 4 points and 8 rebounds in 25 minutes on Monday after Anthony Davis came back. He had posted 13 and 8 and then 15 and 14 in the two games Davis missed on November 6 and 7. The show said he will probably have more quiet games than good ones while Davis plays.
Alex Sarr started but played only 25 minutes for five points and eight rebounds. The show said Sarr is only good when Anthony Davis is out and is not even playing starter minutes.

Alex Sarr started and played 44 minutes in the double-overtime loss to Detroit, posting 30 points and 9 rebounds for 51.25 DraftKings points. The show said he played more mainly because Kyshawn George fouled out, not because Anthony Davis fouled out late.

Alex Sarr played 27 minutes on November 15 with the rest of Washington's starting lineup intact. The show said 27 minutes is the expected number for him and that he has come around after a slow start.
Alex Sarr scored 25 points with three blocks after scoring 30 points in his previous game. The show said his usage has gone up after a poor start, though his shooting will not stay this hot.
Alex Sarr (illness) and Tre Johnson (low back soreness) are questionable against Houston, which would open minutes for Bilal Coulibaly.

Alex Sarr had a poor line but still played 31 minutes as Washington lost its eighth straight game. The show said his overall activity has been trending up and that the playing time is the part to trust.
Rookie Allen Graves scored a career-high 13 points in 18 minutes off the bench Wednesday against Boston.
He sat Wednesday with low back soreness, and Steven Adams (calf) and Marcus Smart (forearm) were also out. Fred VanVleet scored 24 as Houston moved to 5-0.
Alperen Sengun is questionable tonight at Dallas with low back soreness after sitting Wednesday. Fred VanVleet scored 24 with Sengun out and is off the report for the first night of a back-to-back.
He missed Friday with low back soreness, and Clint Capela started at center with 11 rebounds and five assists in 30 minutes. Houston has not posted its injury report for Saturday yet.

The show said Alperen Sengun has an easy matchup on Nov 13 because Utah is without Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkic, leaving Mo Bamba and Jaxson Hayes to guard him. Houston's own centers Clint Capela and Steven Adams are still out.

Houston is without Clint Capela and Steven Adams, and Marcus Smart is serving a league suspension. Alperen Sengun has played 35 to 39 minutes in three of his last four games, but Houston is a 17.5-point favorite over a Utah team missing Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr.
Alperen Sengun scored 43 points on 17-of-24 shooting with 12 rebounds in 37 minutes against Utah on Friday, November 13.

Alperen Sengun played 28 minutes in a 28-point win against WAS on Sunday, 8 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 12 minutes of garbage time. His 45.0 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

Alperen Sengun had 23 points and 7 rebounds in 30 minutes at Miami on 11/16, and the show said he was cooking until Houston fell well behind. The show called Wednesday's matchup against Indiana a great spot for him.
Amen Thompson had 19 points, seven rebounds, four assists, and two blocks in 29 minutes. The show said it still wants more playing time for him, but the game was not close late.

Amen Thompson ran the point for Houston on November 15 with Fred VanVleet resting and Marcus Smart suspended, and he played 29 minutes with 26 points, seven rebounds and seven assists. The show said he is much more productive when he is the point guard, but his role has not been that this season. VanVleet returned on November 16.

Amen Thompson played 29 minutes in a 28-point win against WAS on Sunday, 6 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 12 minutes of garbage time. His 49.2 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

Amen Thompson is questionable for Houston at Indiana. The show said he plays massive minutes when active, and he logged 41 minutes on 11/13. The show said that if he sits, Reed Sheppard, Marcus Smart and Tari Eason all get a sizable minutes bump; when he missed 11/16, Eason started and played 27 minutes.

Amen Thompson is questionable at Indiana with left knee soreness after missing Monday. Indiana is without Tyrese Haliburton, Andrew Nembhard is questionable with hip soreness, and T.J. McConnell is probable and getting more minutes.

Andre Drummond has played 12 to 16 minutes off the bench in each of his last six games. The show said he can produce 30 fantasy points in 18 minutes but is only a large-field tournament dart, especially if Cup-game minutes tighten.
Andrew Nembhard has started every game with Tyrese Haliburton out since 10/26, and he played 34 minutes with 12 assists on 11/09. The show said his steals are low for a guard.

Andrew Nembhard has played 34 minutes in each of Indiana's last two games with Tyrese Haliburton out, posting 12 and 10 assists. The show said Indiana is running him out for a lot of minutes and called him playable at $7,000.
Andrew Nembhard played 34 minutes and had six assists on November 13. The show said he has to be rostered now but becomes a back-end player once Tyrese Haliburton returns.

Andrew Nembhard was moved from questionable to out for tonight on the NBA's 05:30 PM injury report. He had averaged 34 minutes over his last 5 games, so those minutes go to teammates; the injury page lists who gains.
The show said Andrew Wiggins picked up most of Pelle Larsson's playing time on November 13, although he did not do much with it. Wiggins played 32 minutes off the bench and scored 8 points.

Andrew Wiggins has come off the bench since 11/08 after starting earlier in the month. The show said he has complained to the media about his role and that Pelle Larsson's absence could flip his minutes back up over time.

Andrew Wiggins played 34 minutes off the bench with Bam Adebayo leaving early and Pelle Larsson out, and he scored 17 points with three blocks. The show noted he took only nine shots and doubted he would do much more even if Adebayo misses time.

Kentavious Caldwell-Pope was in Philadelphia's rotation ahead of Anfernee Simons on November 10 and scored 0 points in 16 minutes. Simons scored 17 points in 18 minutes, which the show called his first big game in a long time.

Anfernee Simons scored 17 points in 23 minutes off the bench with five threes against Toronto. He and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope combined for 28 bench points, and the show said the pair made 8 of 11 threes.
Anfernee Simons played just 15 minutes because of foul trouble and had 12 points with nothing else. The show said he is a hot-and-cold scorer who does not fit well on a good team.

Anthony Black averaged about 35.6 minutes over his five games from November 5 to November 13, with 16.2 points, 6.2 rebounds, 6.0 assists and 2.2 steals in that stretch per the box scores. The show said this role has an expiration date because Jalen Suggs is back and Paolo Banchero will return at some point. Suggs came off the bench on November 13 and started on November 16, and Banchero was ruled out again on November 16.

Anthony Black started and played 37 minutes but scored just 5 points for 19 DraftKings points against Milwaukee. The show called it a long overdue clunker after an intense hot streak and said he is still a play.

Anthony Black had 20 points and 7 assists in 33 minutes against Boston on 11/16 in Jalen Suggs' first game back in the starting lineup. The show said it never expected Suggs' return to hurt Black much.
He missed Friday with his ankle sprain, and the show doubts he plays both games of the back-to-back that continues Saturday at Oklahoma City.

He has missed two straight games with his ankle sprain and is questionable again at Detroit. Kyshawn George scored 33 and 38.25 DK points in the two games without him, and the show expects George to be the most popular play if Davis sits.
Anthony Davis had 21 points and 13 rebounds in 34 minutes Wednesday, and Washington hosts Detroit on the second night of a back-to-back. The Wizards have not posted their injury report yet.
Anthony Davis had 30 points and 15 rebounds in 44 minutes against Detroit before fouling out, according to the show. The game went to double overtime, which helped his minutes.

Anthony Edwards is out again after knee surgery, and Donte DiVincenzo is also out. Ayo Dosunmu has started and played 30 to 39 minutes in each of his last six games, and LaMelo Ball has scored 20 or more in three straight.
Anthony Edwards remained out on 11/14 and has not played since 10/26. The show said he will be out a long while and does not expect anything to change for Minnesota until he returns.

Anthony Edwards and Donte DiVincenzo are ruled out again for Chicago's visit. Ayo Dosunmu keeps starting, and Minnesota is a 14.5-point favorite against a Bulls team on the second night of a back-to-back.
He is ruled out tonight (arthroscopic procedure on his right knee).
Asa Newell had surgery Tuesday to repair a plantar plate tear in his left big toe, hurt November 4. He will be re-evaluated in about four months.

Thompson played 43 minutes and posted his first triple-double on November 12, but he played only 18 minutes on November 14. The show said he has a very large role whenever games are competitive and he stays out of foul trouble.

Ausar Thompson was Detroit's key defender Tuesday, with five steals, and he also ran offense with 12 assists. He closed the comeback win as Detroit played without Jalen Duren, Duncan Robinson, Taurean Prince and Ronald Holland II.

With Luka Doncic out, Austin Reaves scored 43 points in 37 minutes in a road win at Detroit. The show said the Lakers used extra screens to get Reaves switches away from Ausar Thompson. Reaves was later ruled out for the November 9 game with an illness.

Austin Reaves played 25 minutes in a 11-point win against MIL on Wednesday, 12 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 8 minutes of garbage time. His 35.2 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

Austin Reaves is ruled out at Phoenix with a left heel bruise (X-rays negative, day-to-day). Collin Sexton is questionable after stitches over his eye, while Quentin Grimes is available with a splint on his finger.
He is ruled out tonight. Grimes is the main beneficiary and could post top-70 numbers in those games.
Reaves is questionable tonight against Utah with the Lakers on the second night of a back-to-back. The show said he has been banged up lately and leaned toward his prop unders.
He is questionable tonight vs UTA.

Anthony Edwards has not played since 10/26, and Ayo Dosunmu has started and logged 30 to 39 minutes in each of his last six games. He scored 26 points in 30 minutes on 11/08 with four threes. The show said he has been one of the best fantasy players in the league since Edwards went down, but that the role will not last once Edwards returns.

Ayo Dosunmu played 27 minutes in a 39-point win against DAL on Thursday, 9 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 12 minutes of garbage time. His 26.5 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.
With Anthony Edwards, Jaylen Clark and Jonathan Kuminga all out, Ayo Dosunmu played 39 minutes Tuesday, including the whole fourth quarter, up from 30 the night before.

With Isaiah Jackson out on Nov. 8, Miller played 20 minutes off the bench and posted 12 points, five rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks. The show said he is the deep-league backup center option if Jackson misses again.

Miller has moved into a real bench role with 20 minutes and 12 points on Nov. 8 and 16 minutes and 13 points on Nov. 10, after playing 12 or fewer minutes in each prior game. The show called him impressive and is watching how the Clippers find minutes for him.
Bam Adebayo played 34 minutes on Nov. 8 and 37 minutes on Nov. 10. The show said he was awful to start the season but has picked it up while playing huge minutes, and it called him fairly priced.

The show said Bam Adebayo's usage rate is down about four points from last year while playing next to Giannis Antetokounmpo, and that his points and rebounds are lower. He is averaging about 2.2 steals per game through November 11, which the show called a likely mirage that will come back down.

The show said Bam Adebayo has rebuilt his game this season by mostly dropping his three-point attempts and working around the rim, which has pushed his field goal percentage to about 53 percent. It said his high steal rate is driving much of his fantasy value and could fall.

Bam Adebayo played 16 minutes in a 18-point win against HOU on Monday, 20 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 11 minutes of garbage time. His 11.8 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

Bam Adebayo sat the second half Monday with right hip tightness; Miami called it proactive and does not think it is long-term. Giannis Antetokounmpo moved to center and Andrew Wiggins started the second half. Miami next plays Wednesday.
Bam Adebayo is probable Wednesday against Milwaukee with a right hip impingement; Miami's coach said the team was being cautious and does not expect it to linger.

Baylor Scheierman started in Boston's rotating fifth starter spot and played 29 minutes with nine points, seven rebounds, three threes, two steals, and a block. The show said Boston should give him more starts over Jordan Walsh and that he is worth a look in 14-team leagues when a starter sits.

Baylor Scheierman played 18 minutes off the bench on November 15 and had 12 points and two steals. The show said Boston's bench minutes can go to Scheierman, Sam Hauser, Hugo Gonzalez or Jordan Walsh on any given night, which makes any of them hard to trust.

Baylor Scheierman scored 19.2 of his 27.2 DraftKings points in garbage time of a 37-point win against DAL on Sunday, when the lead was 20 or more late. His line is bigger than his normal role; expect less in a close game.
Baylor Scheierman played only 11 minutes and scored zero points one game after a strong night, so the show admitted its call on him did not work.
Ben Sheppard is having surgery Wednesday to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee.
Ben Simmons is out for the season.
The show said Benedict Mathurin gets a bump with Dejounte Murray out while Murray waits to be traded. The show framed it as a deeper-league bump rather than a major role change.

The rookie has averaged about 22 minutes and 12 points from Oct. 29 through Nov. 10, and the show said Oklahoma City is using him more than most people expected. The show said the addition of Nique Clifford and the eventual return of Jalen Williams will cut into his minutes.
Bilal Coulibaly returned on Nov. 11 after missing Nov. 9 and played 25 minutes off the bench. The show said he is off the injury report and offers steals, blocks and a few assists.
The Clippers signed Blake Wesley to a 10-day contract using a hardship exception because of their injuries.

Bobby Portis played 23 minutes after Bam Adebayo left with hip tightness, up from 14 to 20 minutes in his previous six games. The show said Portis is Miami's only other true center and should get at least 26 to 28 minutes if Adebayo sits, which has typically made him fantasy viable.
Bones Hyland scored 14 points in 13 minutes off the bench Sunday against Utah.
Bones Hyland scored 24 points with 8 assists in 23 minutes off the bench on Nov. 12 (45.75 DK). The show said he is playing with very high usage and gets extra run in blowouts.

Bones Hyland has played 21 to 23 minutes in his last two games with Anthony Edwards out, up from 10 to 13 minutes earlier in the month. The show said Jaylen Clark's injury on November 14 and blowouts helped him, and it does not think his recent efficiency is sustainable.

The show said Bones Hyland should get 16 to 20 minutes off the bench while Anthony Edwards and Jaylen Clark are out. He played 23 and 21 minutes in his two games before Monday, but only 13 minutes on Monday night. The show said his strong recent numbers will not hold long term.
Braden Smith started again for Indiana but did not start the second half and played only 10 minutes. The show said he did not appear to play in the second half.
Braden Smith started on Nov 7 and Nov 9 but played only 12 and 10 minutes and scored zero points in both games. The show said he started the first half on Nov 9 and did not play again.
Bradley Beal (knee) has not played yet this season and is still recovering.

Brandin Podziemski played 22 minutes in a 38-point loss against SAS on Friday, 11 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 12 minutes of garbage time. His 14.8 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

The show said Brandin Podziemski will be great with Stephen Curry out. Per the show, last season he averaged 17.5 points, 6.7 rebounds and 4.9 assists per 36 minutes with Curry off the floor, and this season's smaller sample is 18.2 points and 5.7 assists per 36. The show suggested taking about 10 percent off those rates as a fair expectation.

Brandon Ingram (heel surgery) and Bradley Beal are out again for the Clippers. Darius Garland is playing through a back issue, and Keaton Wagler has played 25 to 28 minutes off the bench in each of his last three games.

The show said Brandon Ingram is nearing a return from his Achilles injury and could in theory debut against Utah on November 17, but it would not count on that. The Clippers then go on a four-game road trip that includes San Antonio on Thursday and Dallas on Saturday. The show expects a long ramp-up and said he is probably at least a week or two from being lineup-worthy.
The show said Brandon Ingram might be back for the Clippers' next game. His return would cut into minutes for wings like Kris Dunn, Derrick Jones Jr. and Keaton Wagler.

The show said Miller's usage, on-ball rate, and potential assists are all up this season. The show said his shooting is well below his expected numbers and should improve, even though he is not a great shooter.

He is out Monday with a hip strain, Kon Knueppel is out at least four more weeks and Dennis Schroder is out at least two weeks. Moussa Diabate is questionable, and the show named Hannes Steinbach as the fill-in if he sits.

Brandon Miller, Kon Knueppel and Dennis Schroder are all out at Phoenix, while Moussa Diabate and Grant Williams are probable. Sion James and Grayson Allen started Monday, and Allen scored 27 points with six threes.
Brandon Miller is off the injury report after missing two games with a hip strain, with Kon Knueppel and Dennis Schroder still out with hamstring strains.

Charles Lee benched Brandon Miller in overtime against the Lakers on 11/17, holding him to 32 minutes. The show said Miller had been dinged up and was turning the ball over, and it viewed the benching as frustrating but not a lasting concern.

Brandon Williams has a mild left hamstring strain and is out at least a week. Golden State is also without Jimmy Butler III, Kristaps Porzingis, Moses Moody and Gary Payton II at Houston, which is missing Clint Capela and Steven Adams.
Brandon Williams is out again on Monday, November 16, because his strained left hamstring is taking longer than the one week first expected.
Brayden Burries has kept starting for Milwaukee, but his minutes have ranged from 19 to 29. The show said his role depends on whether he plays well enough for the team to keep him on the floor.

Brayden Burries started and played 29 minutes on November 15 in a game where starters Tyler Herro, Myles Turner and Kyle Kuzma played 20 to 23 minutes. The show said his minutes go up in blowouts while the veterans' minutes go down, which gives him a relatively safe floor.

Ryan Rollins is out for Milwaukee tonight with an illness. The show said that opens a little more opportunity for Burries on paper, but it said his real ceiling comes only when Tyler Herro and Jaime Jaquez Jr. are also out.

Brice Sensabaugh jumped to 23 and 27 minutes in his last two games after playing 10 to 14 minutes in his previous five. The show said it does not firmly believe the bump will last because Will Hardy keeps changing his bench groups, and it called him a risky scoring stream who could still drop back to about 14 minutes.

Sensabaugh's bench minutes have climbed to 23, 27 and 30 over his last three games while Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. are out. The show said Utah does not have many options and that he has a real NBA skill, although it hoped he would draw less ownership on 11/17.

Brice Sensabaugh played all 12 minutes of the fourth quarter Tuesday and scored 25 of his 40 points in it, as Utah turned a close game into a 132-107 win. He is still coming off the bench behind Josh Green, who started and played 13 minutes.

Brice Sensabaugh played the whole fourth quarter Tuesday and scored 25 of his 40 points in it as Utah pulled away from the Clippers. His bench minutes have climbed four straight games with Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. out, but Utah has not posted its report for tonight's back-to-back at the Lakers.

Brook Lopez came off the bench in the Clippers' first six games and has started every game since November 2, with Isaiah Jackson now coming off the bench. The show said Lopez has the first crack at center minutes and scored 20 points in each of his competitive starts with near-starter minutes; he then scored 26 points in 31 minutes as a starter on November 13. The show expects Yanic Konan Niederhauser (right foot surgery) to return in one to two weeks and probably become the starting center after a ramp-up, so Lopez may hold the job for about a month.

Brook Lopez has started at center ahead of Isaiah Jackson in every game since at least November 8, and he scored 26 points on November 13. The show said the switch to the starting lineup sparked his run, but it expects the frontcourt to get crowded when Yanic Konan Niederhauser returns from foot surgery.

Brook Lopez played 29 minutes on November 15 and had eight assists even though he shot poorly. The show said he was the only Clippers starter who held up in that game, finishing plus two. The show called him the clearest hold among the Clippers starters.

Brook Lopez played 23 minutes in a 25-point loss against UTA on Tuesday, 5 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 5 minutes of garbage time. His 39.0 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

Bryce McGowens scored 12.8 of his 17.8 DraftKings points in garbage time of a 34-point loss against BKN on Wednesday, when the lead was 20 or more late. His line is bigger than his normal role; expect less in a close game.

Buddy Hield played 25 minutes off the bench on November 13 and stayed on the floor late while playing well. The show said Chicago will need bench production without Caleb Wilson and called him a stream option on light days.

Buddy Hield had been out of Chicago's rotation behind Jordan Hawkins, but he played 25 and 20 minutes on November 13 and 14 after Caleb Wilson went down. The show said his usage is up, but it does not trust his three-point shooting to hold.

Cade Cunningham played only 27 minutes on Nov 9 with 17 points and 7 assists, and the show said he was in foul trouble. The show said Daniss Jenkins is a ball-dominant facilitator, and his move into the starting lineup takes a little away from Cunningham.

The show said Cade Cunningham carries about a 30% usage rate and a 38% assist rate this season with about 56.5% true shooting. It projected him at about 51 DK points on 11/12 and called him the best stud play on the slate even though Washington plays at a slow pace.
Jalen Duren (hamstring) and Isaiah Joe (hip) are both ruled out at Miami. Cade Cunningham played 48 minutes Thursday and scored 52 points, and Paul Reed played 38 minutes at center.

Cade Cunningham was moved from questionable to out for tonight (right knee soreness) on the NBA's 07:30 PM injury report. He had averaged 37 minutes over his last 5 games, so those minutes go to teammates; the injury page lists who gains.
Detroit is on the second leg of a back-to-back at New Orleans on Wednesday. The show said Cade Cunningham does not usually rest on back-to-backs and liked the matchup.

Caleb Martin has started and played 33 and 34 minutes in Dallas' last two games, up from about 20 minutes before that. The show said he is a very low-usage player but is playable while he keeps starting.
Caleb Wilson played only 15 minutes on November 11 and has missed Chicago's last two games. The show said he went down, which opened minutes for Patrick Williams and Buddy Hield.
Cam Johnson was out on Oct. 28 and is expected to return fairly soon.
Ty Jerome and Scotty Pippen Jr. are both questionable Saturday against Sacramento. Spencer has moved ahead of Pippen in the rotation and had eight assists in 23 minutes Thursday.

The show said Spencer steps up whenever Scotty Pippen Jr. or Ty Jerome is out. Pippen has not played since October 29, and when Jerome sat on November 14, Spencer started and played 34 minutes. The show said Spencer is worth using while either guard is out.

Cam Spencer has moved into the starting lineup with Ty Jerome out, starting on 11/14 and 11/16 after coming off the bench while Jerome played. His minutes jumped to 34 and 32 in those two starts, up from the low 20s in his bench role. The show said Spencer is the preferred Memphis guard over Javon Small because he plays more minutes, with points, assists and threes as his steady categories.

Cam Spencer should start again Wednesday because Ty Jerome is out. In the two games Jerome missed, Spencer started and played 34 and 32 minutes for 34.3 and 33.0 DraftKings points. Off the bench before that, he played 17 to 24 minutes.

Spencer has started Memphis's last two games while Ty Jerome and Scotty Pippen Jr. were out, playing 34 and 32 minutes, and both are out again tonight. The show said Javon Small covered Spencer's bench minutes on 11/16 and the two also shared the floor, especially in the fourth quarter. The show called Spencer a core play even though his price has risen.

Cameron Boozer is averaging about 16 points, 9.8 rebounds and 5.5 assists in about 32 minutes through November 11. The show said his field goal percentage and his defensive stats (about half a steal and half a block per game) are the weak spots, and it expects him to improve as the rookie learning curve passes.

Cameron Boozer played 25 minutes in a 31-point win against NOP on Friday, 9 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 5 minutes of garbage time. His 36.0 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

Cameron Boozer has started every game, but his minutes have slipped from 33 in his 11/9 and 11/11 games to 25 and 29 in his last two. The show said his shooting efficiency has been among the worst of the rookie class, but it liked him as a bounce-back with Ty Jerome out.

Cameron Boozer made seven threes and scored 29 points on 11/16, but he played only 29 minutes because Memphis was comfortably ahead. The show said he normally settles into a 32 to 33 minute role and liked him against Cleveland with Evan Mobley out and Ty Jerome out on his own side.

With Ty Jerome out on Monday, Cameron Boozer took on more of the scoring and set a season high with 29 points, making 7 of 13 threes, including two during the 10-0 third-quarter run that tied the game.

Memphis is short again at Cleveland: Ty Jerome (right hip) and Isaiah Stewart (illness) are out, and GG Jackson had foot surgery Tuesday and will be re-evaluated in about three months. Boozer, Cam Spencer and Jerami Grant carry more of the load.
Cameron Carr made his debut Sunday and played 1 minute late in the game without scoring.

Cameron Johnson has started and played 29 to 34 minutes in each of his last four games. He has averaged a little over 12 points in that stretch. The show said he is close to being a must-roster player.
Cameron Johnson scored 23 points with four threes in 30 minutes. The show called it his first big game of the season and said his hot shooting makes it somewhat fake.
Cameron Johnson picked up five fouls and still played 27 minutes, but he had nine points and no rebounds. The show said to move on from him.

Carter Bryant scored 14.5 of his 15.8 DraftKings points in garbage time of a 38-point win against GSW on Friday, when the lead was 20 or more late. His line is bigger than his normal role; expect less in a close game.
The show said Wallace is presumably out for the season. He has not played since Oct. 25.
Cedric Coward played 33 minutes and scored 54.5 DraftKings points on 11/14 with Ty Jerome out. The show said he has been incredible lately, although it wished his 6,500 salary was a little lower.

The show said Cedric Coward's minutes swing from game to game, but his rebounding has been consistently strong, partly because Zach Edey has been off the floor so much. Over his last 11 games before November 16, the box scores show 14.4 points, 9.0 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game.

The show said Cedric Coward has been excellent without Ty Jerome. He has scored 41 or more DraftKings points in each of the two games Jerome missed (11/14 and 11/16). The show also liked his rebound numbers against a Cleveland team missing Evan Mobley and possibly Peyton Watson.

The show said Cedric Coward has been very productive for fantasy even on relatively low usage. He had 18 points, 8 rebounds and 6 assists in 27 minutes on only 10 shots, and the show doubted the rebounding pace will hold all season.

Charles Bassey's minutes have climbed to 20, 23, 14, 11 and 18 over the five Warriors games from November 1 through November 9, after he played only 2 to 9 minutes in earlier games. The show said there is a center role for him with Kristaps Porzingis out, since Draymond Green and Al Horford do not play big minutes there. The show expects about 15 to 16 minutes a night with strong per-minute rebounds and blocks.

Bassey has played 11 to 23 minutes as a backup big, with Kristaps Porzingis, Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody, and Brandon Williams all ruled out on Nov. 11. The show said he likely needs one more frontcourt injury, such as to Al Horford, to reach a steady 12 to 15 minute role. Brandon Williams is out with a left hamstring strain.

Charles Bassey has played between 11 and 20 minutes off the bench in Golden State's recent games. The show said he would be a must-add at 22 minutes a night, but the Warriors change lineups too often to trust his role.

Chaz Lanier played 25 minutes on Tuesday only because Detroit was missing Ronald Holland II and Duncan Robinson, and he scored just 3 points. The show said his minutes should mostly disappear as injured players return.
He is out 8 to 10 weeks with a small patellar tendon tear, so Isaiah Hartenstein and Aday Mara take on the frontcourt minutes.
Chet Holmgren is out eight to 10 weeks with a small patellar tendon tear and will not need surgery. He has not played since Oct. 25.
He is ruled out tonight. Mara had 11 points, 10 rebounds and two blocks in 20 minutes Monday with Holmgren out.

Chris Cenac Jr. jumped into the rotation for 12 minutes with Neemias Queta resting. The show said he looked very athletic and that Joe Mazzulla talked him up after the game, so he is someone to keep in mind.

Christian Anderson had his best game as a pro with 16 points, four threes and two steals while Dennis Schroder was out with a hamstring strain. The show said it hopes Charlotte keeps him in that role after Schroder returns.

The show said Anderson is finally playing well, but his minutes are limited and should shrink further as Charlotte gets healthier. He has played 16 to 18 minutes in each of his last three games off the bench.

Christian Braun started and played 28 minutes against New Orleans, and he was Denver's third-best DraftKings scorer behind Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray for the third time in the last six games. The show said Braun is the third Nugget with value more often than not, but it doubted that holds all season.

CJ McCollum played 32 minutes on November 13 after playing 21 to 25 minutes in four of his previous five games. Kingston Flemings left that game with a back injury after 17 scoreless minutes. The show said the question is whether McCollum moves from a 24-minute role to about 27 minutes while Flemings is struggling or unavailable.

CJ McCollum played 32 minutes off the bench at Chicago after Kingston Flemings left early, scoring 20 points with 5 rebounds and 5 assists. The show said he has been a high-usage bench player for a few games and will play more in the short term.

CJ McCollum moved back into Atlanta's starting lineup on November 15 with Kingston Flemings out with a lumbar back issue, and he played 30 minutes. He scored 20 points with four steals, and the show said he went nine for nine at the free-throw line. The show treated Flemings as day-to-day.
The show said CJ McCollum will be out for about a month for Atlanta, and he is ruled out tonight with a left calf strain. Kingston Flemings is also out for the Hawks.
Capela started on Oct. 30 with Alperen Sengun and Steven Adams out, but he is now out himself. He missed Nov. 2 with a right ankle sprain.
Coby White started for Charlotte against Cleveland and played 20 minutes, scoring 10 points with nine assists. Royce O'Neale came off the bench and scored 10 points in 23 minutes.

Coby White has played 16, 18 and 16 minutes in Charlotte's last three games after coming into the season hurt. The show said this is injury management rather than a skill issue, and that his minutes could jump to 24 to 29 on any night, possibly Nov. 9 with Schroder, Knueppel and Miller out. The show admitted he will probably still play around 18 minutes and called it a speculative low-owned dart.
The show said Charlotte plays only five games over the next 14 days, which is a very light schedule. This limits how many DFS slates the Hornets appear on during that stretch.

Coby White has been on a slow ramp-up since returning from injury, playing 16, 18, 16, 20 and 20 minutes in his five games from November 2 through November 12. He had nine assists on November 9 and scored 21 points in 20 minutes on November 12. The show said it expects him to reach about 23 to 24 minutes by the middle of next week, with fuller value roughly a week after that.

White played 16, 18 and 16 minutes in his first three games and then 20 minutes in each of his next three. He scored 21 points on November 15 even with Brandon Miller and Naz Reid playing. The show said it is waiting for his minutes to rise to around 24 before trusting him at $5,400.

Coby White's minutes limit was raised to 26 minutes on Tuesday after 20 minutes in each of his previous three games, and he did not play in overtime. The show said his production in limited minutes points to big numbers once the limit goes away.

Cody Williams started in place of the injured Jonathan Kuminga on Tuesday but played only 13 minutes. Trey Lyles got the real minutes at power forward, playing all 12 minutes of the fourth quarter and closing the one-point win.

Collin Gillespie outplayed Jalen Green and got more minutes than him on November 12, playing 27 minutes off the bench. The show said his bench role makes him harder to trust, but the minutes are trending in his favor.

Collin Gillespie played 27 minutes off the bench against Charlotte and scored 13 points. The show said this was a high-water mark and that he got a few extra minutes because the reserves won the game while Jalen Green played poorly. Jordan Goodwin also got extra minutes and played 24.

Collin Gillespie's minutes are rising off the bench, with 28 on 11/15 and 27 on 11/12 after 20-24 in the three games before. The show said Phoenix needs a true point guard and is starting to recognize that playing him more helps.

Collin Gillespie played 26 minutes off the bench and has played 26 to 28 minutes in each of his last three games. The show said Phoenix looks bad without a true point guard and Gillespie is the only one on the roster, so it expects his minutes to stay at 25 or more unless the Suns trade for a guard.

The show is watching whether Collin Gillespie keeps playing more minutes than Jalen Green, though it does not expect him to take Green's starting job. Gillespie out-minuted Green off the bench on 11/10, 11/12, and 11/15, while Green played 27 minutes to Gillespie's 26 on 11/16. The show also wants to see how Jordan Goodwin, who played 20 minutes on 11/16, fits into that rotation.
Collin Murray-Boyles returned on Nov. 11 and started, playing 20 minutes after missing Nov. 9. The show expects him to be available Thursday.

Collin Murray-Boyles stayed in Toronto's starting lineup at center when Scottie Barnes returned on November 15, and he played 40 minutes in an overtime game. The show said this answers the question of who starts at center once Barnes plays power forward. The show warned that Toronto's back-to-back on Tuesday and Wednesday could muddy the next data point.
Collin Murray-Boyles started at center over Jakob Poeltl on Sunday and played 40 minutes, including all of overtime, while Scottie Barnes returned from a four-game groin absence with 36 minutes.

Collin Murray-Boyles started again over Jakob Poeltl, who came off the bench for the second straight game. The show said Toronto's coach and beat reporters described this as a matchup-based lineup against Karl-Anthony Towns, so it does not expect Murray-Boyles to stay in the starting role.

Collin Murray-Boyles started and played 33 minutes against the Knicks, which the show said is the workload it wanted to see. He grabbed only one rebound, but he added three blocks and a steal. The show said he is in great shape with Jakob Poeltl moving to the bench.
The show listed Murray-Boyles as one of the leading center plays at his price tonight with Scottie Barnes out. It said he would look even better if RJ Barrett, who is questionable, is also ruled out.

Collin Sexton has come off the bench in every game and played 24 minutes on November 15. The show said he has been a letdown as the second-unit ball handler and needs to defend better. The show does not expect his minutes to get high enough to matter unless that changes.

Flagg played 28 minutes in a 130-93 win over Brooklyn on Nov. 8 and still had 25 points and 12 assists, because Dallas pulled him early in the fourth quarter. The show said he is still too cheap at $9,900 on Nov. 9 and is close to triple doubles.

Cooper Flagg has played 40, 40, 33, 28 and 39 minutes in his last five games, including 73 DK points in 39 minutes on 11/9. The show said Kyrie Irving being healthy cuts into Flagg's role on paper and that Minnesota is one of the best defenses in the league. The show also said Flagg is overpriced at $10,100 but is the only stud under 10% ownership on the 11/12 slate.

Cooper Flagg played 27 minutes in a 37-point loss against BOS on Sunday, 6 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 12 minutes of garbage time. His 30.2 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.
The show said the Dallas coach told the media that Cooper Flagg gets lazy on defense when his shots are not falling. The show liked Flagg under $10,000 and hoped the comment fires him up.

Corey Kispert played 16 minutes off the bench on November 15 while Luguentz Dort played 18 and Aaron Wiggins played 24. The show said the wing minutes will keep rotating among Dort, Wiggins and Kispert and that Dorian Finney-Smith has not really been in the rotation.

Craig Porter Jr. played 28 minutes off the bench on November 14 while Cleveland's regular starters sat. The show called him a very good producer when he gets minutes, but it said Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor are both ahead of him in the rotation right now.
The show said Oklahoma City waived Dalen Terry a few days after signing him, as part of the move to get Nique Clifford. Terry played five and six minutes in his two games with the Thunder.
He played 37 minutes Friday, and the show labeled him and Robert Williams III doubtful for Saturday against San Antonio on the back-to-back.

The show said Lillard's usage is around 26 percent, close to the 27 percent he posted the last time he played a full season. The show expects it to rise a little more with Ja Morant and Shaedon Sharpe injured. Ja Morant is out at least four weeks with a left hamstring strain.

Damian Lillard scored 25 points with four threes in only 24 minutes in a blowout. The show said Portland's many blowouts have held his minutes down to about 28 per game and that he usually sits the whole fourth quarter when a game is not close. The show expects his minutes and free-throw percentage to rise.

Damian Lillard has started all 10 of his games and averages about 29 minutes and 20 points in the box scores. The show said blowouts have cut his minutes, with his scoring near 22 points in competitive games and much lower in lopsided ones. He played just 20 minutes on Nov 7 and 24 minutes on Nov 10.
Lillard played both games of the back-to-back against the Thunder, scoring 18 points in 32 minutes on the second night. The show said his usage is not as high as expected.

The show called November 13 a big usage game for Damian Lillard, who took 18 shots and 11 free throws in 33 minutes with Ja Morant out. The show said his free throw percentage is climbing toward 90 percent.
Damian Lillard played 31 minutes on the second night of the back-to-back Tuesday, up from 24 Monday, when Portland emptied its bench late.

Portland plays Minnesota again on the second night of a back-to-back, and the Blazers had not posted their injury report Tuesday morning. Lillard played only 24 minutes Monday after Portland emptied its bench down 19 late.

Daniel Gafford played only 18 minutes in each of his Nov. 4 and Nov. 6 starts and 19 minutes on Nov. 8. The show called the minutes worrying with Morez Johnson Jr. emerging, and it said Dallas also has P.J. Washington and eventually Dereck Lively II in the frontcourt mix.
Daniel Gafford started but played only 20 minutes and had 8 points, 2 rebounds and 3 assists. The show said foul trouble caused the low minutes and that this was his third poor game in a row.

Daniel Gafford has played 20 minutes or fewer in each of his last five games, including 16 minutes on Nov. 12. The show said foul trouble and blowouts played a part but questioned whether he goes back to being a 24-minute player.

Daniel Gafford played 19 minutes as a starter on November 15 after suffering a stinger in his previous game. The show said he is still useful in about 21 minutes a night and needs only around 22 minutes to provide value, so it is not giving up on him.

Jenkins scored 31 points off the bench on Nov 8 and moved into the starting lineup the next night in place of Paul Reed. He has started all three Detroit games since then and played 35 to 42 minutes in each. The show said he is worth streaming for as long as he stays in the starting lineup.

Jenkins has played at least 32 minutes in each of his last four games and has started the last three. He topped 40 DraftKings points on 11/08 and 11/09. The show said he is the best Piston to play after Kevin Huerter because Detroit's thin roster keeps his minutes high.

Daniss Jenkins played 38 minutes and scored 25 points in his fifth straight start (he has started every game since 11/9). The show said he should keep starting because John Collins is a poor fit, and Detroit needs Jenkins as an extra ball handler.

Detroit came back from 14 down to end San Antonio's 12-game winning streak with Kevin Huerter starting for Duncan Robinson and Ausar Thompson running more offense. Detroit plays at New Orleans on the second night of a back-to-back and has not posted its injury report.

Danny Wolf has started each of Brooklyn's last four games and played 28 to 36 minutes, even with Mikel Brown Jr. and Nolan Traore back. The show said it does not understand why he still starts, but it noted he keeps getting good minutes.

Danny Wolf went back to the bench on 11/16 and played only 11 minutes after starting four straight games with 28 to 36 minutes. The show said Brooklyn's coach seems to pick night to night who plays, rotating among Wolf, Nolan Traore, Keon Ellis and Noah Clowney.
Darius Acuff Jr. scored 32 points with 5 rebounds, 10 assists and 3 threes in 39 minutes on Nov 8. The show said his usage was about 31 percent and he is a top-40 head-to-head player this season.

Darius Acuff Jr. has played between 33 and 42 minutes in each of his last six games, and he scored 32 points with 10 assists on Nov. 8. He has three double-doubles this season, including two 30-point double-doubles (Oct. 29 and Nov. 8). The show called him the top point guard play against Orlando, which it said ranks 25th in defense, whether or not Domantas Sabonis plays.

Darius Acuff Jr. took 25 shots for 26 points on November 15 and committed nine turnovers. The show said coach Doug Christie has given him a license to shoot freely as part of his development and suggested this is frustrating Domantas Sabonis.
The show said there is a risk the Clippers limit his playing time later in the season if the team keeps losing and has injuries.

Garland played 35 to 37 minutes in each of his last two games and scored at least 41 DraftKings points in three of his last four. The show said his minutes and production have risen as the Clippers have played more competitive games and won more often.

Darius Garland scored 27 points with seven assists while Brandon Ingram remained out after heel surgery. The show said it would like more usage from him during Ingram's absence and that his turnovers have been high.

The show said no Clipper plays big minutes, with Darius Garland the leader at 33 minutes per game and Rui Hachimura next at 29. The box scores match, with Garland at 33.2 and Hachimura at 29.0 minutes per game. The show said this makes a large minutes load for a returning Brandon Ingram unlikely.

The show said Utah does not help off, which is good for high-usage guards and bad for shooters, and called the Nov. 17 game one of the best Darius Garland spots he will get. Garland has played 35 and 37 minutes as a starter in his last two games. The show also liked Keaton Wagler as a sneaky value after he played 28 minutes off the bench on Nov. 15.

Lauri Markkanen has not played since November 6, and Darryn Peterson has taken 19 to 21 shots in each of the four games since. The show said Peterson should be owned in every league with Markkanen hurt.

Peterson has taken between 19 and 21 shots in each of his last five games while Lauri Markkanen has been out. The show said Utah is letting him shoot as much as he wants and that his price is still too low for that volume.

Darryn Peterson has played 33 or 34 minutes in each of Utah's last three games as a starter while Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. are out. The show said it really likes both Peterson and Keyonte George on Nov. 17 and expects George to play in the low 30s in minutes.

Davion Mitchell handed out 17 assists in 39 minutes on November 13. The show said it expected Giannis Antetokounmpo to have the ball in his hands more, but Mitchell has been running the offense and playing phenomenally.

The show said Davion Mitchell has settled in as Miami's secondary scorer and main facilitator behind Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. He has started every game in the box scores, playing 29 to 43 minutes, and had 17 assists on November 13.

Davion Mitchell has been Miami's starting point guard and has scored 41 or more DraftKings points in three straight games, including 16 points, 10 assists and 4 steals against Houston on 11/16. The show said he does it every night and is still priced at $7,000.

Day'Ron Sharpe played only 25 minutes on 11/16 because of foul trouble. The show said not to worry about it and that Sharpe has settled into a steady role alongside Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr.

De'Aaron Fox played 17 minutes in a 38-point win against GSW on Friday, 11 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 12 minutes of garbage time. His 15.8 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

De'Aaron Fox (left hip soreness) and Devin Vassell are questionable for San Antonio against Golden State, and Tobias Harris is out. Dylan Harper had 18 points and 10 assists in 36 minutes Wednesday and would handle more of the offense if Fox sits.
De'Aaron Fox returned to the starting lineup Tuesday after missing Sunday's game and played 34 minutes, and he was on the floor to close the game.

De'Aaron Fox returned to the starting lineup on Tuesday after missing 11/15 and played 34 minutes but scored only 6 points. The show said Fox and Stephon Castle should both see their usage and assist rates rise while Dylan Harper is out.
De'Aaron Fox missed Sunday's game but is not on San Antonio's injury report tonight. Tobias Harris (calf) is likely out until early December.
The show said De'Andre Hunter and Zach LaVine both missed Sacramento's last game but it has no real worries about either of them for Wednesday.

With Stephen Curry out, De'Anthony Melton moved into the starting lineup on November 13 but played only 18 minutes. The show said Curry's abdominal injury will likely keep him out at least a month and that Golden State's roster is very thin without him. The show expects Steve Kerr to push Melton toward 30 or more minutes if he keeps shooting well.

De'Anthony Melton came off the bench for 21 minutes on 11/16 while LJ Cryer started, after Melton had started the game before. The show said the last two games without Stephen Curry were blowouts and that Melton played 27 to 28 minutes in competitive games Curry missed earlier, on 10/24 and 11/1, so it expects more minutes in a close game such as the next one against Dallas.

Dean Wade started every game this season that LeBron James or Joel Embiid missed, playing 28 minutes on Oct. 24, 37 minutes on Oct. 25 and 30 minutes on Oct. 31, while coming off the bench at about 18 to 23 minutes otherwise. The show said Wade probably starts and plays 30-plus minutes if LeBron or Embiid sits and could get 90-plus minutes over Philadelphia's next three games.

Dean Wade played 35 minutes off the bench on November 15 with Joel Embiid out. The show said everyone else on Philadelphia got more usage without Embiid but Wade did not, and that he does not reach fantasy value no matter how many minutes he plays.
Dean Wade played 35 minutes off the bench with Joel Embiid out, but he took only 5 shots. The show said his ultra-low usage makes sustained value almost impossible even when the minutes are there.

Wade started with LeBron James out and played 32 minutes with 11 rebounds. The show said Wade is generally the next man up when James sits. It also said he is a much better real-life player than a fantasy player.

Dean Wade has played 32 to 35 minutes in his last three games and should keep a big role with Jaylen Brown out Wednesday. His DraftKings output swings hard, though: 16.3 points in 34 minutes on November 12 and 29.8 in 32 minutes on Monday. He scores little himself, so he needs rebounds and threes to hit value.

Dean Wade was moved from questionable to out for tonight on the NBA's 06:15 PM injury report. He had averaged 28 minutes over his last 5 games, so those minutes go to teammates; the injury page lists who gains.

The show expects Dean Wade's minutes to rise with Jaylen Brown out and said he should get at least 30 minutes. Wade has played 32 to 35 minutes in each of his last three games, starting on 11/12 and 11/16 when LeBron James sat and playing 35 minutes off the bench on 11/15 when Joel Embiid sat. The show said Kentavious Caldwell-Pope or Anfernee Simons could also take Brown's starting spot.
DeAndre Jordan started at center for New Orleans on November 13 and played 17 minutes. The show said he started for no clear reason and should not be added.
DeAndre Jordan started at center on November 13 but did not play on November 14 once Yves Missi returned to the starting lineup. The show said Jordan is now out of the rotation.
The show said the Pelicans are trying to trade him.

Dejounte Murray started but had only 6 points, 3 rebounds and 3 assists in 28 minutes on Nov 8. The show said his usage was about 12 percent and that he has been pushed aside since returning from the birth of his child.

Dejounte Murray started but played only 18 minutes and had 12 points, 3 rebounds and 1 assist. The show said foul trouble limited him, his usage was higher than in recent games, and he is outside the top 100 over the last two weeks.

The show said the Pelicans are trying to trade Dejounte Murray and want to give Jeremiah Fears as many touches as he can handle. Murray has cooled off with 7, 6, and 12 points in his last three games, and he played only 18 minutes on Nov 9. The show said his steals keep his value steady even with a usage rate around 20 percent.

Dejounte Murray started and played 28 minutes but had only five points and four assists. The show said he is barely getting the ball and is outside the top 140 over the last two weeks despite heavy minutes.

Dejounte Murray has requested a trade away from New Orleans, and he did not play on November 13 because of a left ankle sprain. The show said it does not expect a quick trade because few teams are hunting for a point guard and the price will be a sticking point. He was also ruled out for November 14 with the ankle sprain.
Dejounte Murray has not played since November 11 and missed the Pelicans' games on November 13 and 14. The show said his trade request is the reason he is not playing.

Dejounte Murray has not played since 11/11, and the show said New Orleans shut him down about four days ago amid trade talk. The show cited reports that teams expect the Pelicans to attach draft assets in a deal, and it noted the Suns were linked but have denied interest. The show guessed he could be out about a month.
DeMar DeRozan came off the bench for 20 minutes and had eight points and four assists. The show said Denver is using him only as a bench player.

Deni Avdija played 34 minutes with 24 points, six rebounds and eight assists. The show said he is the only Blazer getting full minutes in blowouts because he is still on the floor early in the fourth quarter.

items.text: Quentin Grimes has started all three games Austin Reaves has missed and scored 47 with 10 threes in Tuesday's overtime win, including 21 in the fourth quarter. Reaves was set to test his heel Wednesday morning before tonight's back-to-back against Utah, and the Lakers called Walker Kessler's Tuesday absence precautionary.

Jaylen Brown is out at Orlando with a left hamstring strain he felt late Monday. Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid take on more of the offense, and Dean Wade, Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope pick up the wing minutes.

Brice Sensabaugh played the whole fourth quarter Tuesday and scored 25 of his 40 points in it as Utah pulled away from the Clippers. His bench minutes have climbed four straight games with Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. out, but Utah has not posted its report for tonight's back-to-back at the Lakers.

Memphis is short again at Cleveland: Ty Jerome (right hip) and Isaiah Stewart (illness) are out, and GG Jackson had foot surgery Tuesday and will be re-evaluated in about three months. Boozer, Cam Spencer and Jerami Grant carry more of the load.

Atlanta has six players out at Oklahoma City, including CJ McCollum and Kingston Flemings, so the ball handling falls to Jalen Johnson, Dyson Daniels and RayJ Dennis. Asa Newell had toe surgery Tuesday and will be re-evaluated in about four months.

Amen Thompson is questionable at Indiana with left knee soreness after missing Monday. Indiana is without Tyrese Haliburton, Andrew Nembhard is questionable with hip soreness, and T.J. McConnell is probable and getting more minutes.

Detroit came back from 14 down to end San Antonio's 12-game winning streak with Kevin Huerter starting for Duncan Robinson and Ausar Thompson running more offense. Detroit plays at New Orleans on the second night of a back-to-back and has not posted its injury report.
Golden State is very thin at Dallas: Stephen Curry, Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody, Kristaps Porzingis and Brandon Williams are out, and Draymond Green (elbow) and Al Horford (back) are questionable.
